target: Forecast the local sorted unit responsible for the next occupied complete 1 ms bin if it contains precisely one observed spike. Censor the last forecast of each interval. All spikes in complete occupied bins, including unresolved targets, update the next forecast. No inference of fine event order from multiple events in a bin.
initial_source_screen: Palmer et al., Dryad 10.5061/dryad.4qrfj6qm8 v3, version id 334025, provides natural movie responses binned at 16.667 ms for 93 sorted retinal ganglion cells. Do not infer 1 ms spike times from this material.
source: Loback et al., Dryad 10.5061/dryad.1f1rc v1, version id 1813, file 10783 error_robust_mode_data.zip, 87524253 bytes, MD5 f34c92b51f2abcc3ff965500176ff9fc; Zenodo record 4976473 lists that DOI and checksum. 10 kHz recording. Verify native stored units, start/end markers and candidate axis before any score.
selection: Include the repeated natural movie experiment and, as separate stimulus-domain checks, checkerboard and moving bar experiments in this file when stimulus-repeat starts and lengths can be verified. Sort original repeats by acquisition onset and use the first ten full documented repeats, with a common 10 s prefix starting at each repeat onset (all available if fewer). A repeat presented on a common time-aligned spike array can use its original source index. Exclude the nonrepeated movie from primary repeat-level macro comparisons because it has no common repeated segment. Never select on spike rates, identities, scores or signs. Report unavailable experiments and any source inconsistencies. Experiments are separate; only describe independent retinas/animals if source states the mapping. Never map IDs between recordings.
clock: Use the absolute sample clock and all complete intervals with bins (left,right]; use exact integer sample-to-millisecond ceiling on a documented 10 kHz sample clock or the pinned reference millisecond_edges on seconds. Forecast after the current bin closes. Reset counts and traces per repeat. No partial leading/trailing bin. Respect recorded interval boundaries; report any spike observations exactly on boundaries. No labels, stimulus inputs, upcoming gap or target calibration.
roster: All sorted cell entries in the source experiment, including all inactive entries. Electrode count is not candidate count. Report available, active, resolved target counts as well as unresolved multi-spike targets.
model: JDS-SingleDay-JS14/01 five frozen weights, no retraining, no unit ID matching or fitted salamander offsets. weights.json SHA256 25f9d22ee284b794c1a4f7019587b6e4b92631ab04ff9664266045aa4718ecad, benchmark.py SHA256 3514e7925fd9c833ab5f939513991eadb04b246cab3d63ee320e807410251f61, original protocol SHA256 c0c04287d26d8b1ab7996053adaee26b858ce4b2a0f0110d88726a4c4a06bc08.
outputs: Use the original shared_model, online_rate, recency and uniform rules with float64. Report per-repeat and equal-repeat trial macro, pooled and unit-balanced top1 tie fractional, natural-log loss, midrank and 1-10/11-100/101+ issue ordinals. Paired equal-repeat log loss differences and descriptive 5000 within-recording repeat bootstrap 95% intervals with seed 20261121. Define rare units prospectively as cells with 1 through 10 resolved target spikes in the selected repeats within each recording, scoring each comparator on identical rows, with rare row and unit counts; absent groups stay empty. Add equal-recording macro as descriptive if multiple files qualify. Do not extrapolate to independent animals without animal keys. Compare only to the reported rodent regimes and overlapping baseline definitions.
freeze: Selection and analyses fixed before obtaining/opening any held outcome values. No refit or hyperparameter selection. Report every frozen result, including unfavorable results.
